fact_statement: UCIL (Union Carbide India Limited, the plant operator) had decoupled the two warning-siren systems, so the factory's own siren could sound for a routine leak without the public siren alerting the surrounding community.
anchor_quote: The two siren systems had been decoupled from one another in 1982, so that it was possible to leave the factory warning siren on while the public one remained inactive.

fact_statement: Tank E610 held nearly 30% more liquid MIC than UCC's own safety regulations permitted for a single tank.
anchor_quote: At the time of this failure, tank E610 contained 42 tons of liquid MIC.

fact_statement: The safety test being run on reactor no. 4 the night of the disaster did not require sign-off from either the reactor's chief design authority or the nuclear safety regulator.
anchor_quote: According to the existing regulations, such a test did not require approval by either the chief design authority for the reactor (NIKIET) or the nuclear safety regulator.

fact_statement: Test data going back to 1977 had already shown a potentially catastrophic O-ring flaw in the Solid Rocket Boosters, and neither NASA nor Morton Thiokol fixed the known defect before the 1986 launch.
anchor_quote: Test data since 1977 had demonstrated a potentially catastrophic flaw in the SRBs' O-rings, but neither NASA nor SRB manufacturer Morton Thiokol had addressed this known defect.

fact_statement: Titanic's wireless operators received multiple real ice warnings the night of the sinking but the ship kept sailing at roughly 22 knots when the iceberg was sighted.
anchor_quote: Titanic's wireless operators received seven warnings of sea ice leading up to the night of 14 April, but was travelling at a speed of roughly 22 knots (41 km/h; 25 mph) when her lookouts sighted the iceberg.

fact_statement: A 2011 US government report found defective cementing of the well was a major cause of the spill and assigned most responsibility to BP, while also faulting Transocean and Halliburton.
anchor_quote: A US government report, published in September 2011, identified defective cementing of the well as a major cause and assigned most responsibility to BP, while also faulting rig operator Transocean and contractor Halliburton.

fact_statement: A separate White House commission also concluded the disaster stemmed from cost-cutting decisions and inadequate safety systems at BP and its partners.
anchor_quote: Earlier in 2011, a White House commission similarly blamed BP and its partners for cost-cutting decisions and inadequate safety systems.

fact_statement: Blasting work was underway in the area believed to be the ignition point of the explosion, after an earlier attempt to widen a gallery there had failed the previous day.
anchor_quote: Blasting was being done in the area believed to be the source of the explosion, after initial attempts to widen a gallery had been abandoned the previous day for lack of success.

fact_statement: Local residents had formally complained to their council about the coal-slurry tip being dumped behind the Pantglas schools well over a year before the disaster.
anchor_quote: Complaints had been made by residents to Merthyr Tydfil County Borough Council, who corresponded with the NCB between July 1963 and March 1964 on the topic of the "Danger from Coal Slurry being tipped at the rear of the Pantglas Schools".

fact_statement: Investigators found Massey Energy had failed to properly maintain the mine's ventilation systems, letting methane accumulate to dangerous levels before the explosion.
anchor_quote: Investigators later faulted Massey Energy for failure to properly maintain its ventilation systems, which allowed methane levels to increase to dangerous amounts.

fact_statement: New Zealand's own Prime Minister later apologised to victims' families specifically for the government's weak regulations and inadequate mine-inspection regime.
anchor_quote: then-Prime Minister John Key said he would apologise in person to the families of those killed for the Government's weak regulations and inadequate inspection regime.

fact_statement: Internal Samarco documents leaked in 2016 showed the company had been warned, more than a year before the collapse, that the tailings dam could fail.
anchor_quote: In January 2016, leaked internal documents from 14 months before the disaster revealed that Samarco had been warned about the possibility of the dam collapsing.

fact_statement: The initial roof collapse at the mine on 28 December was never reported to mining inspectors, even though doing so was legally mandatory.
anchor_quote: They also revealed that the collapse of 28 December was not reported to mining inspectors, as was mandatory.

fact_statement: The mine's declining safety investment traced partly to prior management diverting cash flow from mine operations to corporate expenses and debt rather than exploration or development.
anchor_quote: These included low silver prices and the lack of regular and consistent exploration and development due to prior management shifting cash flow from the mine to corporate expenses, debt and other projects.

fact_statement: An earlier safety audit had recommended keeping the pumps in automatic mode whenever divers were not working near the intakes, matching practice on the neighbouring Claymore platform, but Piper Alpha never implemented it.
anchor_quote: A recommendation from an earlier audit had suggested that a procedure be developed to keep the pumps in automatic mode if divers were not working in the vicinity of the intakes, as was the practice on the Claymore platform, but this was never implemented.

fact_statement: A permit-handover breakdown meant the on-duty custodian was never told that a critical pressure safety valve had been removed for maintenance before the fatal gas release.
anchor_quote: As the on-duty custodian was busy, the engineer neglected to inform him of the condition of pump A.

fact_statement: The official inquiry found the ferry's capsizing traced to three specific individual failures: the assistant bosun not closing the bow doors, the chief officer not checking they were closed, and the captain leaving port without confirming their state.
anchor_quote: It found the capsizing was caused by three main factors—Stanley's failure to close the bow doors, Sabel's failure to make sure the bow doors were closed, and Lewry leaving port without knowing whether the bow doors were closed.

fact_statement: Exxon Shipping Company had failed to keep the ship's collision-avoidance radar system in working order, which if functional would have warned the crew of the impending collision with Bligh Reef.
anchor_quote: Exxon Shipping Company failed to properly maintain the Raytheon Collision Avoidance System (RAYCAS) radar, which, if functional, would have indicated to the third mate an impending collision with the Bligh Reef by detecting the radar reflector placed on the next rock inland from Bligh Reef for the purpose of keeping ships on course.

fact_statement: A later investigation found that the ferry's seaworthiness certificate was invalid because the required regulatory inspection of the bow visor parts had never actually been carried out.
anchor_quote: A further investigation found that the certificate of seaworthiness was incorrect since no inspection of the bow parts was done as per regulations, otherwise this would have led to the discovery of the flaws in the visor.

fact_statement: Shortly after the collision, the ship's own engine-room chief personally warned Captain Schettino that the hull had a large irreparable tear letting water flood the generators and engines.
anchor_quote: A few minutes after the impact, the head of the engine room warned the ship's captain, Francesco Schettino, that the hull had an irreparable tear of 35 metres (115 ft) through which water entered and submerged the generators and engines.

fact_statement: Spanish investigators concluded the primary cause was the KLM captain deciding to take off believing he had clearance, despite the Pan Am crew's own radio call that they had not yet confirmed clearing the runway.
anchor_quote: An investigation by Spanish authorities concluded that the primary cause of the accident was the KLM captain's decision to take off believing that air traffic control (ATC) had issued takeoff clearance and that the Pan Am Boeing had cleared the runway, despite the latter radioing that they would "report when clear of the runway".

fact_statement: A faulty repair Boeing technicians made after an earlier tailstrike, seven years before the crash, eventually failed catastrophically and destroyed the plane's hydraulic systems and flight controls.
anchor_quote: When the faulty repair eventually failed, it resulted in a rapid decompression that ripped off a large portion of the tail and caused the loss of all hydraulic systems and flight controls.

fact_statement: After an earlier, unrelated fire incident, the NTSB had already recommended the FAA require smoke detectors and fire-suppression systems in class D cargo holds like the one that caught fire on Flight 592.
anchor_quote: After Flight 132, the National Transportation Safety Board (NTSB) recommended to the FAA that all class D cargo holds be fitted with smoke detectors and fire-suppression systems.

fact_statement: The DC-10's crash-landing traced to an unnoticed manufacturing defect in the tail engine's fan disk, which caused the total loss of the aircraft's flight controls.
anchor_quote: On July 19, 1989, the McDonnell Douglas DC-10 serving the flight crash-landed at Sioux Gateway Airport in Sioux City, Iowa, after suffering a catastrophic failure of its tail-mounted engine due to an unnoticed manufacturing defect in the engine's fan disk, which resulted in the loss of all flight controls.

fact_statement: The FAA formally revoked Boeing's own authority to certify individual MAX aircraft as airworthy and separately fined the company for pressuring its own designated safety inspectors.
anchor_quote: The FAA revoked Boeing's authority to issue airworthiness certificates for individual MAX airplanes and fined Boeing for exerting "undue pressure" on its designated aircraft inspectors.

fact_statement: Investigators traced two of the early Comet crashes to structural failure from metal fatigue in the airframe, a phenomenon not yet well understood by engineers at the time.
anchor_quote: Two of these were found to be caused by structural failure resulting from metal fatigue in the airframe, a phenomenon not fully understood at the time; the other was due to overstressing of the airframe during flight through severe weather.

fact_statement: A residents' campaign group had publicly warned, over a year before the fire, that people could be trapped in the tower because it had only one entrance/exit and cluttered corridors.
anchor_quote: In January 2016, GAG warned that people might be trapped in the building if a fire broke out, pointing out that the building had only one entrance and exit, and corridors that had been allowed to fill with rubbish, such as old mattresses.

fact_statement: A cladding option with better fire resistance was rejected for the tower's refurbishment specifically because of its cost.
anchor_quote: An alternative cladding with better fire resistance was refused due to cost.

fact_statement: The day before the collapse, factory owners on the upper floors ignored visible warning signs (cracks) and sent workers back in anyway, even though the shops and bank on the lower floors had already closed over safety concerns.
anchor_quote: The shops and the bank on the lower floors immediately closed, but the garment factory owners on the upper floors ignored the warnings and the workers returned to work the following day.

fact_statement: The National Bureau of Standards' final report found the walkways' design gave them only minimal capacity to support even their own weight, let alone a crowd.
anchor_quote: The NBS's final report cited structural overload resulting from design flaws where "the walkways had only minimal capacity to resist their own weight".

fact_statement: Investigators flagged the bridge's main truss system for lacking structural redundancy, meaning a single structural failure anywhere in it carried a disproportionately high risk of full collapse.
anchor_quote: The report also noted a concern about lack of redundancy in the main truss system, which meant the bridge had a greater risk of collapse in the event of any single structural failure.

fact_statement: Investigators found the bridge's southern support stays failed suddenly because of corrosion damage that had built up over time.
anchor_quote: The southern stays reportedly gave way explosively due to corrosion and damage.

fact_statement: The dam's chief engineer had originally recommended twelve sluice gates, but this was criticized as excessive and the actual number built was cut down to five.
anchor_quote: He had recommended 12 sluice gates for the Banqiao Dam but this was criticized as being excessive and the number was reduced to five.

fact_statement: The disaster followed years in which ENEL and the Italian government concealed reports and dismissed real evidence that the mountainside above the reservoir was geologically unstable.
anchor_quote: This event occurred after ENEL and the Italian government concealed reports and dismissed evidence that Monte Toc, on the southern side of the lake, was geologically unstable.

fact_statement: The dam operator's own engineers had run model-based experiments in mid-1962 specifically studying the effects a further landslide from the unstable mountainside could have on the reservoir.
anchor_quote: In July 1962, SADE's own engineers reported the results of model-based experiments on the effects of further landslides from Monte Toc into the lake.

fact_statement: The Fukushima disaster's direct cause was the 2011 Tōhoku earthquake and tsunami, which knocked out grid power and damaged nearly all of the plant's backup power sources.
anchor_quote: The direct cause was the Tōhoku earthquake and tsunami, which resulted in electrical grid failure and damaged nearly all of the power plant's backup energy sources.

fact_statement: A 2003 internal BP audit had already found a 'checkbook mentality' and blame culture eroding safety performance at the refinery, with poor asset condition and no meaningful action plans in place, years before the explosion.
anchor_quote: An internal BP audit conducted in 2003 found that a "checkbook mentality", blame, and status culture eroded HSE as well as general performance; the condition of assets and infrastructure was poor; management had not created meaningful action plans; and that there were insufficient resources.

fact_statement: BP's cost-cutting after acquiring the refinery specifically targeted maintenance spending, starting in the early 1990s.
anchor_quote: Starting in the early 1990s, Amoco and later BP made substantial budget cuts, especially affecting maintenance expenditure.

fact_statement: The temporary pipe modification that caused the Flixborough explosion had its mechanical engineering risks overlooked by the managers who approved it.
anchor_quote: Mechanical engineering issues with the modification were overlooked by the managers who approved it, and the severity of potential consequences due to its failure were not taken into account.

fact_statement: OSHA had not inspected the West Fertilizer Company plant since 1985, decades before the explosion.
anchor_quote: At the time of the incident, the Occupational Safety and Health Administration (OSHA) last inspected the plant in 1985.

fact_statement: The accident was worsened by real design flaws in the control room, including poor control layout, multiple similar-looking alarms, and no clear indicator of coolant level or the stuck-open relief valve's actual position.
anchor_quote: During the accident, those inadequacies were compounded by design flaws, such as poor control design, the use of multiple similar alarms, and a failure of the equipment to indicate either the coolant-inventory level or the position of the stuck-open PORV.

fact_statement: A testing institute had told Deutsche Bahn management as early as 1992 -- six years before the disaster -- about its concerns over possible wheel-tyre failure in the wheel design later linked to the crash.
anchor_quote: It was revealed later that the institute had told the DB management as early as 1992 about its concerns about possible wheel–tyre failure.

fact_statement: London Underground's own director of operations had warned, a few years before the fire, that built-up paint on the escalators might pose a fire hazard, but this warning went unheeded.
anchor_quote: A few years before the fire, the Underground's director of operations had warned that the accumulated paint might pose a fire hazard.

fact_statement: Railtrack itself had already warned, in a December 1999 letter, that its own existing track specification was insufficient to guard against the type of rail fatigue that caused the crash.
anchor_quote: The problem was known about before the accident; a letter from the infrastructure company Railtrack in December 1999 warned that the existing Railtrack Line Specification was insufficient to guard against this type of fatigue.

fact_statement: JR West drivers who ran late faced financial penalties and punitive retraining programs involving humiliating manual labor tasks like weeding and grass-cutting.
anchor_quote: Drivers for JR West face financial penalties for lateness as well as being forced into harsh and humiliating retraining programs known as nikkin kyōiku (日勤教育, "dayshift education"), which include weeding and grass-cutting duties during the day.

fact_statement: The official Ministry of Transport report found the Perth express train's driver had passed both a caution signal and two separate danger signals before the fatal collision.
anchor_quote: The Ministry of Transport report on the crash concluded that the driver of the Perth train had passed a caution signal and two danger signals before colliding with the local train.

fact_statement: North Korea's own state news agency attributed the explosion to careless electrical contact during the shunting of railway wagons loaded with ammonium-nitrate fertilizer.
anchor_quote: KCNA, the state news service, apparently confirmed the Xinhua report by stating the incident was "due to the electrical contact caused by carelessness during the shunting of wagons loaded with ammonium-nitrate fertilizer".

fact_statement: The official 1915 Board of Trade inquiry attributed the collision to two signalmen's neglect of the standard signalling rules.
anchor_quote: An official inquiry, completed on 17 June 1915 for the Board of Trade, found the cause of the collision to be neglect of the rules by two signalmen.
